root_cause.text: is_bpf_migration_disabled() in sched_ext unconditionally treated task_struct->migration_disabled == 1 for current as a BPF-prolog artifact, even on non-CONFIG_PREEMPT_RCU kernels where the BPF prolog never calls migrate_disable(), causing real migration-disabled tasks to be misclassified as migratable.
root_cause.evidence: The patch changes is_bpf_migration_disabled() from always returning `p != current` when `p->migration_disabled == 1` to doing that only under `IS_ENABLED(CONFIG_PREEMPT_RCU)`, and the commit/CVE state that “Without CONFIG_PREEMPT_RCU, the prolog never touches migration_disabled,” so the old unconditional `p == current` check was “a false negative,” allowing a migration-disabled task to be dispatched to a remote CPU.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix is_bpf_migration_disabled() to account for CONFIG_PREEMPT_RCU so the current task is not misclassified when BPF prolog does not actually disable migration.
intent_record.what: The change updates the comment above is_bpf_migration_disabled() to clarify that BPF prolog migration disabling occurs only when CONFIG_PREEMPT_RCU is enabled, and modifies the function so that when p->migration_disabled == 1 it conditionally checks p != current only if IS_ENABLED(CONFIG_PREEMPT_RCU); otherwise it returns true directly, while all other cases still return p->migration_disabled.
intent_record.how: At runtime, this makes is_bpf_migration_disabled() treat migration_disabled == 1 as unambiguously indicating a truly migration-disabled task on kernels without CONFIG_PREEMPT_RCU, instead of incorrectly treating the current task as not migration-disabled. On kernels with CONFIG_PREEMPT_RCU enabled, it preserves the existing special handling for the current task because BPF prolog may have temporarily disabled migration.

grouping_result.intent: Fix is_bpf_migration_disabled() to account for CONFIG_PREEMPT_RCU so the current task is not misclassified when BPF prolog does not actually disable migration.

relevance_review.reason: The change directly fixes the exact root cause: is_bpf_migration_disabled() now considers CONFIG_PREEMPT_RCU so current->migration_disabled == 1 is only treated as a BPF-prolog artifact when that prolog actually disables migration, preventing misclassification of real migration-disabled tasks.

candidates.rationale: This unconditionally treats migration_disabled == 1 on the current task as a BPF prolog artifact, misclassifying genuinely migration-disabled current tasks as migratable on kernels where the BPF prolog does not call migrate_disable().
This special-case condition is the basis of the flawed logic: it assumes count 1 needs reinterpretation for current without accounting for CONFIG_PREEMPT_RCU, leading to the incorrect branch.

vuln_statements.explanation: This unconditional return causes current with migration_disabled == 1 to be treated as not migration-disabled, assuming the count of 1 is always a BPF prolog artifact. On non-CONFIG_PREEMPT_RCU kernels, that assumption is false because the BPF prolog does not call migrate_disable(), so genuinely migration-disabled current tasks are misclassified as migratable.

bic_trace_step.code_snippet:
commit 55ed11b181c43d81ce03b50209e4e7c4a14ba099
Author: Andrea Righi <arighi@nvidia.com>
Date:   Sat Sep 20 15:26:21 2025 +0200

    sched_ext: idle: Handle migration-disabled tasks in BPF code
    
    When scx_bpf_select_cpu_dfl()/and() kfuncs are invoked outside of
    ops.select_cpu() we can't rely on @p->migration_disabled to determine if
    migration is disabled for the task @p.
    
    In fact, migration is always disabled for the current task while running
    BPF code: __bpf_prog_ente
bic_trace_step.reason: The snippet is sufficient because it includes the newly introduced helper `is_bpf_migration_disabled()` and the call site in `select_cpu_from_kfunc()`, which is exactly where the migration-disabled determination is made. The vulnerable root cause was that `is_bpf_migration_disabled()` unconditionally treated `p->migration_disabled == 1` for `current` as a BPF-prolog artifact, which is wrong on non-`CONFIG_PREEMPT_RCU` kernels. In this commit's function body, the helper does `if (p->migration_disabled == 1) return p != current; else return p->migration_disabled;`. This means when `p` is `current` and `migration_disabled == 1`, it returns `false`, i.e. it assumes the value came from BPF context rather than real migration disable state. That is the vulnerable construct described in the root cause. However, the commit message and diff indicate this commit is introducing this helper as the intended handling relative to the prior plain `is_migration_disabled(p)` check. So in the context of this commit version, the specific later fix for non-`CONFIG_PREEMPT_RCU` is not present. Therefore the code contains the buggy construct and does not yet contain the complete fix.
